title: ROUTE 161 ACCIDENT
full_story:
A Kinmundy woman and a Centralia woman were injured in a 2-vehicle wreck on Illinois Route 161 west of I-57 near the entrance to Biggies early Wednesday morning.

Marion County Sheriff’s Deputies say 50-year-old Sheryl Watwood of Kinmundy was driving west on Route 161 when she pulled to the shoulder in preparation for making a left turn.  She was blinded by the sun when pulling back across the highway and didn’t see an approaching car driven by 21-year-old Lexie Draper of Centralia.  The two collided with the impact causing the Watwood car to roll over on the passenger side.

Watwood was out of her car and taken to St. Mary’s Hospital in Centralia for treatment of injuries.  Draper was airlifted from the scene by Air Evac to Barnes Hospital in St. Louis for treatment.

title: NOBLE VILLAGE BOARD
full_story:
The Noble Village Council met Monday night in regular session.

Guest Wendy Coles and KaRissa Miller both from Illinois Eastern Community College were present to discuss the villages OSHA complaint.  Coles is the Workforce Education Instructor and Miller is in charge of the financials.  Wendy Coles explained her role to the board as a workforce safety and compliance training instructor.  She implements the needed plans and training that is necessary to be OSHA compliant.  There would be a one-time charge and she would have all the necessary documentation on hand for compliance.  Miller explained that after the board discussed their needs, she would put together the financial/grant information.  If approved for a grant, the cost to the Village, at most, would be 10% of the cost.  Trustees tabled the matter until the next meeting.

Mayor Brad Kessler informed the board that the village has been selected for a remote IMRF Employer Compliance Review.  The Village will also be flushing fire hydrants throughout the Village.  Residents may experience low water pressure and water discoloration while work is being done in their area.

Guest Bill Manuel gave the board an update of the work currently being done at the sewer lagoon.  They are currently prepping for the curtain to be installed.  The board voted to approve purchasing two culverts from DK Tank & Pipes.  One will be 12” X 30’ $223.80 and the other is 12” X 50’ $381.96 with a $100.00 delivery fee.  And, the board approved the closing of North Noble Avenue between Elm and Poplar streets for the May Fest/Car Show that will be held on Saturday, May 2nd.

Residents were reminded that the Easter Egg Hunt will be held in the Noble Park on April 4th at 2 pm and the Clean-up Day is scheduled for April 29th.

title: FLORA LIBRARY PROGRAMS
full_story:
This afternoon Illinois State Treasurer Michael Frerichs’ staff will be at the Flora Public Library to help reunite citizens with missing money and property through the I-Cash program.

In Clay County, an estimated 16,600 people and/or businesses have unclaimed cash or property.  The value exceeds $1,695,000.00.  Statewide, Frerichs secures more than $5 billion in unclaimed cash and property.  The event will be from 2:00 pm to 5:00 pm this afternoon at the Flora Public Library.

In Illinois, the state treasurer is tasked with safeguarding missing money, such as unpaid life insurance benefits, forgotten bank accounts and unused rebate cards.  Illinois holds more than $5 billion in unclaimed property.  The state treasurer is legally required to return the property to the rightful owners no matter how long it takes.  Individuals can search the state treasurer’s database for their name or the name of their business or non-profit at illinoistreasurer.gov/icash.

title: IECC BOARD MEETING
full_story:
The Board of Trustees of the Illinois Eastern Community College met Tuesday, night at Wabash Valley College, Mt. Carmel.

A resolution to formally accept the FY2025 Audit prepared by Martin Hood PLLC was approved and will be submitted to the Illinois Community College Board. The District received a clean and unmodified audit opinion.  The Board also approved the 2027-2029 Academic Calendar as proposed.

The Bid Committee recommendation was approved for acceptance of the bids from Southwestern Travel Group for a total of $55,458 for the TRIO Upward Bound Education Trip, and Bruce Unterbrink Construction, Inc., of Greenville, for a total of $1,345,000 for the Science Lab Renovations at Olney Central College Wattleworth Hall.

Approval of employment was given for David Murphy as Custodian, OCC effective March 30th, and Kera Vinson as Head Volleyball Coach & Student Life Coordinator, FCC, Student Affairs effective May 26th.

Retirement ratifications were approved for Tammie Bohnhoff as Math Instructor, at OCC, Academic Affairs effective August 5th; Rena Gower as Director of Learning Commons, at LTC, Student Affairs effective April 3rd, and Robert Conn as Dean of Instruction, at WVC, Academic Affairs effective March 6th.

The reemployment of Bargaining Unit Faculty for the 2026-2027 Academic Year was approved as presented.

The next regular meeting of the Board of Trustees will be Tuesday, April 21st at 6:15 pm at Frontier Community College.

title: EPA EMERGENCY WAIVER
full_story:
The US Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) issued an emergency fuel waiver allowing the sale of E15 gasoline nationwide this summer, as it has done the past several years.

Through the waiver, EPA is fortifying the domestic gasoline supply chain and providing relief at the pumps ahead of the summer driving season, according to EPA.

The waiver will be in effect from May 1st to May 20th, the maximum number of days allowed under the Clean Air Act.  The agency is expected to issue new waivers, effectively extending the emergency fuel waiver through the summer.

Issued Wednesday, the notice allows fuel industry stakeholders adequate time to transition the fuel distribution system.

Ag Secretary Brooke Rollins said that allowing the summer sale of E15 will deliver a bigger domestic market for farmers.

“While today’s announcement is great news for farmers, year-round E15 is essential for the farm economy, and Congress needs to find a commonsense solution that provides much needed certainty to consumers and farmers,” Rollins added.

One of Illinois Farm Bureau’s priorities has been advocating for permanent year-round E15.  A congressional E15 Rural Domestic Energy Council was formed earlier this year to study and come up with a year-round nationwide E15 proposal, but the group has already missed two self-imposed deadlines to release text.

The emergency fuel waiver will temporarily waive the summer low volatility requirements and blending limitations for gasoline to provide additional flexibility to the fuel marketplace, EPA said.  E15 is currently offered at over 3,000 gas stations nationwide.  Without this action, E15 gasoline cannot be used by roughly half of the country this summer.

title: I-COVER CROP PROGRAM
full_story:
The Illinois Department of Agriculture is relaunching the Infield Conservation for Operationalizing Vital Ecosystem Resilience (I‑COVER) program to encourage early establishment of cover crops through new techniques and technology.

Pre-enrollment begins April 1st for the program, which provides cost-share and financial incentives to producers and landowners who are new to cover crops or who use innovative methods to establish cover crops earlier in the season.  I‑COVER is a three-year program supporting cover crops planted in 2026, 2027 and 2028, funded by IDOA through a $7 million grant from the USDA’s Natural Resources Conservation Service (NRCS) under the Regional Conservation Partnership Program.

“Research shows cover crops strengthen soil health, reduce erosion, improve resilience during drought and help manage pests, weeds and diseases,” said Jerry Costello II, IDOA director.  “This program incentivizes farmers to protect and preserve Illinois soil, which is among the most fertile in the world.”

To protect the financial interests of farmers, the program was paused last summer.  IDOA shared in a press release the department did not want farmers to invest in the I-COVER program without assurance that reimbursements would be available.

According to IDOA, state officials have since worked with USDA NRCS to reopen the program, continuing Illinois’ commitment to soil health initiatives.  All applicants who applied during the previous program period must submit a new application to be considered for funding.

Pre-enrollment and applications are available online.  Visit agr.illinois.gov and select the I‑COVER Program link on the home page.

Pre-enrollment will open at 8 am on Wednesday, April 1st, with applications accepted starting at 8 am on Wednesday, April 15th.  The program closes at 11:59 pm on Friday, May 1st.

Applications will be selected on a first-come, first-served basis by county.  The first qualifying application per county will be prioritized.  If funding remains after the initial application is verified, subsequent applications from that county will be considered in order of receipt.

Eligible acres must not be enrolled in other state, federal or private programs that use state or federal funds to implement cover crops from late summer or fall 2026 through 2028, such as EQIP, CSP or Fall Covers for Spring Savings.  Applicants must maintain control of the land for the duration of the program.

Program funding is subject to the availability of federal funds.
